title: L4 · Cells, DNA & Cell Cycle
subtitle: Organelles, DNA and RNA, protein synthesis, mitosis

lines.text: Picture a Jello fruit salad.
The Jello is the **cytosol**, the watery part.
The fruit is the **organelles**, small organs with specific jobs.
**Inclusions** are things that don't dissolve, like fat and pigment.
The nucleus is the brain of the cell. It holds the DNA.
A double membrane with pores surrounds it. That's the **nuclear envelope**.
Relaxed DNA is **chromatin**. Condensed DNA forms chromosomes.
The **nucleolus** has no membrane. It makes ribosomes.
**Ribosomes** are where proteins are made.
The endoplasmic reticulum is a set of canals for transport.
**Rough ER** is studded with ribosomes. It makes proteins.
**Smooth ER** has no ribosomes. It makes lipids and carbs and breaks down drugs.
The **Golgi** body packages enzymes, hormones and lysosomes.
**Lysosomes** are the suicide sacs.
Their digestive enzymes break down bacteria, viruses and worn-out parts.
**Peroxisomes** neutralize toxins and alcohol.
They are abundant in the liver.
**Mitochondria** produce **ATP**.
Their inner folds are **cristae**. They add surface area.
Mitochondria have a double membrane and copy themselves.
They are abundant in muscle cells.
Two **centrioles** at right angles form the centrosome.
They make microtubules and direct the spindle in mitosis.
**Cilia** are short hairs that sweep substances along, like in the lungs.
A **flagellum** is a long tail. In humans, only sperm have one.
**Microvilli** are tiny fingers that add surface area for absorption.
The cytoskeleton gives the cell shape and support.
Think of a tent.
**Microtubules** are the poles.
**Intermediate filaments** are the medium ropes.
**Microfilaments** are the small ropes.
DNA is a **double helix**, a spiral staircase.
The sides are sugar and phosphate. The steps are bases.
Weak hydrogen bonds pair A with T, and C with G.
A **gene** is a blueprint for one protein. We have about 25 thousand.
RNA is single stranded. It uses **uracil** in place of thymine.
**rRNA** makes ribosomes.
**mRNA** copies a gene and carries the code to the cytoplasm.
**tRNA** reads the code and brings the right amino acid.
Human DNA is 46 chromosomes, 23 pairs.
Replication copies all of it, before mitosis.
It is **semiconservative**. Each new DNA is half old strand, half new.
**Helicase** unzips the strands. **Polymerase** builds the new ones.
**Transcription** makes messenger RNA from DNA. It happens in the nucleus.
**Translation** makes the protein at the ribosome.
DNA is read in triplets. Three bases code one amino acid.
On messenger RNA, a triplet is a **codon**. On transfer RNA, it's an **anticodon**.
Four codons make four amino acids, joined by three peptide bonds.
The cell cycle has two stages: interphase and mitosis.
**G1** is the longest phase. The cell grows to full size.
Some cells never leave G one.
In the **S** phase, DNA is copied.
**G2** is housekeeping before division.
Mitosis splits one mother cell into two daughter cells.
**Prophase** is first and longest. The nuclear membrane breaks down and chromosomes condense.
**Metaphase**: meet in the middle.
**Anaphase**: away to opposite ends.
**Telophase**: the nuclei reform and the spindle falls apart.
**Cytokinesis** pinches the cell in two.
